Karst
Soluble rocks: limestone, gypsum, salt
Process: groundwater dissolution enlarges cracks into cavities
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: US Geological Survey, What is a sinkhole?; https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/what-a-sinkhole. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Sinkhole
Surface drainage: no natural external outlet
Rainwater drainage: typically underground
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: US Geological Survey, What is a sinkhole?; https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/what-a-sinkhole. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Collapse sinkhole
Underground change: cavity enlargement
Collapse trigger: cavity roof can no longer support the overlying land
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: US Geological Survey, What is a sinkhole?; https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/what-a-sinkhole. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Karst drainage
Underground pathways: enlarged fractures and caves
Surface streams: commonly disrupted by the underground drainage network
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: US Geological Survey Circular 1139, Hydrologic Cycle and Interactions; https://pubs.usgs.gov/circ/circ1139/htdocs/natural_processes_of_ground.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.
